title: Palantir CEO says Dario Amodei is not the 'caricature' that Americans might believe him to be
excerpt: Alex Karp continued to drag the AI labs during Palantir's all-hands meeting — while defending one of their leaders, Dario Amodei.
content_html:
Alex Karp continue to drag the AI labs — while defending one of their leaders, Dario Amodei.

The Palantir CEO spent July outlining his thesis for "sovereign AI." Firms should want to keep their data, he said; they shouldn't fork it over to a third-party like OpenAI or Anthropic. (You might remember that testy CNBC interview.)

In an all-hands meeting, Karp continued to lay out his theory — and rip into his AI competitors. He called the companies "wildly unlikable."

"They are actually unwilling to respond to any questions about: How do you build the models without ripping off someone's IP, migrating your alpha to your model, and then competing against them?" he said. "They do this over and over."

As in previous interviews, Karp said that he was speaking for enterprises, not from his personal opinion. He didn't find the AI companies "unlikable," he said.

"I've spent a lot of time with Dario," Karp said, referring to the Anthropic CEO. "He's not the caricature that many people, most Americans, believe."

Tokens have been a sticking point for Karp. The unit of AI measurement determines how much companies pay for the technology. In June, he compared tokenmaxxing — or spending as much on AI as possible — to porn addiction.

Once again, Karp took aim at tokens. He said that Palantir's customers were asking: "Why am I paying for tokens that lead to this weird kind of slop that only makes the least productive people happy?"

Palantir popularized the "forward-deployed engineer" model, making it one of the hottest jobs in tech. Google and AWS have both invested in FDEs; OpenAI created a dedicated organization for them.

Karp said in June that OpenAI ripped Palantir off (poorly). In the all-hands, he painted a graphic picture of the forward-deployed engineers, saying that AI companies needed "FDEs that aren't just masturbating and selling tokens."

"That's what these are actually doing," Karp said. "They sell tokens."

content_html_zh:
亚历克斯·卡普 (Alex Karp) 继续拖累人工智能实验室，同时为他们的领导人之一达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 辩护。

Palantir 首席执行官在 7 月份概述了他的“主权人工智能”论文。 他说，公司应该保留他们的数据；他们不应该将其交给 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 等第三方。 （你可能还记得 CNBC 那次暴躁的采访。）

在一次全体会议上，卡普继续阐述他的理论，并猛烈抨击他的人工智能竞争对手。 他称这些公司“非常不讨人喜欢”。

“他们实际上不愿意回答任何问题：如何在不窃取他人知识产权的情况下构建模型，将你的 alpha 迁移到你的模型中，然后与他们竞争？” 他说。 “他们一遍又一遍地这样做。”

和之前的采访一样，卡普表示他是代表企业发言，并非来自个人观点。 他说，他并不认为人工智能公司“不讨人喜欢”。

“我花了很多时间和达里奥在一起，”卡普说，他指的是 Anthropic 的首席执行官。 “他并不是很多人、大多数美国人所相信的讽刺漫画。”

代币一直是卡普的症结所在。 人工智能的衡量单位决定了公司为该技术支付的费用。 6 月，他将 tokenmaxxing（即尽可能多地花在人工智能上）与色情成瘾进行了比较。

卡普再次瞄准了代币。 他说 Palantir 的客户会问：“为什么我要花钱购买代币，而这会导致这种奇怪的结果，只会让效率最低的人感到高兴？”

Palantir 推广了“前沿部署工程师”模式，使其成为科技领域最热门的工作之一。 Google 和 AWS 都投资了 FDE； OpenAI 为他们创建了一个专门的组织。

卡普 (Karp) 在 6 月份表示，OpenAI 击败了 Palantir（效果很差）。 在全体会议上，他描绘了前沿部署工程师的形象，表示人工智能公司需要“不仅仅是自慰和销售代币的 FDE”。

“这就是他们实际上正在做的事情，”卡普说。 “他们出售代币。”
